title: Introduce debounce-aware async validation and live error announcements for inputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our form inputs currently mix immediate client-side validation with unthrottled async server checks. This causes noisy UI updates, redundant network calls on fast typing, and confusing screen-reader announcements (duplicate or out-of-order errors).

Goal: Design a predictable, accessible validation flow for text fields and selects that: (1) reduces redundant async requests via a debounce-aware validation service, (2) surfaces clear, stable validation states visually and via ARIA for screen readers, and (3) respects reduced-motion and token-driven timings.

This ticket covers the UX patterns, accessibility behavior, recommended token values for debounce/animation, and handoff signposts for engineering to implement a library-level validation helper used by our Form primitives.
acceptance_criteria:
[1] There is a documented validation flow describing local sync checks, debounced async checks, and final submission validation.
[2] A single, small ARIA live region pattern is specified so screen readers receive exactly one clear announcement per validation pass.
[3] Token recommendations provided: debounce intervals (default and compact), animation durations, and visual timing adjustments for reduced-motion.
[4] Prototype in Figma showing the states (idle, validating, valid, client-error, server-error) and how inline messages collapse/expand without layout shift.
[5] Engineering has a clear API sketch (validateNow(), cancelPending(), subscribeStatus) and test cases for race conditions.
[6] User testing notes from 3 accessibility reviews are attached and changes are incorporated.
design_notes:
- Use a two-tier debounce: typing-debounce (e.g., 300ms default) for background async validation and submit-debounce (100ms) to avoid blocking instant submit interactions.
- Prefer a single polite ARIA live region per form (role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\") updated only when a validation run finishes to avoid interleaved announcements.
- Inline error messages should be associated with inputs via aria-describedby and include a stable id so announcements reference the same node across updates.
- Visual tokens: --validation-debounce-default: 300ms; --validation-debounce-compact: 150ms; --validation-anim-duration: 120ms; --validation-anim-ease: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1). Respect prefers-reduced-motion by setting duration to 0 and crossfading content.
- For selects and complex widgets, ensure the validation helper can accept a custom compareKey so cached async results don't leak across distinct logical values.
- Show a subtle inline spinner only when an async validation run is pending longer than 200ms to avoid flicker on fast networks.
decisions:
- Chosen a polite ARIA live region over assertive to avoid interrupting typing and screen reader announcements.
- Debounce defaults emphasize user experience for fast typists; shorter debounces available in compact/token overrides.
- Will centralize validation caching at the form-level rather than input-level to enable deduplication for cross-field validations (e.g., username/email uniqueness checks).
- Design accepts slight latency for async checks in favor of reducing request volume and improving announcement clarity.
tradeoffs:
- Longer debounce -> fewer network calls, but slower feedback for server-side constraints (e.g., username uniqueness). We mitigate by showing optimistic client-side hints and a clear pending state.
- Single live region simplifies announcements but requires careful timing to ensure errors map clearly to inputs; engineering must maintain stable ids.
- Adding a shared validation helper increases abstraction surface for devs; we will provide a lightweight migration guide and examples.
- Inline spinner threshold adds complexity but reduces visual noise; implementation must be tested across mobile CPU/network conditions.
rollout_plan:
1) Finalize design tokens and hand off to ENG (ETA 2 weeks).
2) ENG implements validation helper in components lib behind a feature flag.
3) Migrate core form components (TextField, Select, TextArea) in a canary release for internal apps.
4) Run accessibility regression tests and 3rd-party keyboard/screen-reader checks.
5) Flip feature flag and monitor errors/latency metrics for 2 weeks.
6) Publish guidelines and code samples in the component docs.
(Feature flag name: validation-service-v2)
testing_notes:
- Unit tests required for: debounce timing, cancellation behavior, caching behavior, aria-live content ordering, and reduced-motion.
- Accessibility smoke tests: NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS with focus on announcement ordering when multiple fields validate simultaneously.
- Performance tests: network call counts for a 100-typist-simulation across default and compact debounce settings.
- Manual QA: Ensure no layout shift when inline messages appear/disappear; verify aria-describedby attributes persist across updates.
